explanation.text:
The failed run launched `udhcpc` while `eth0` was down, so DHCP remained in the foreground reporting “Network is down” [T0B36:<RANGE>udhcpc: sendto: Network is down
udhcpc: read error: Network is down, reopening socket</RANGE>]. It then repeatedly sent network and SSH commands into that still-running process rather than successfully interrupting it and returning to a shell [T0B42:<RANGE>C-c
ip link set eth0 up
ip addr show eth0
udhcpc -i eth0
echo 'PermitRootLogin yes' >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config
echo 'PasswordAuthentication yes' >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config
udhcpc: read error: Network is down, reopening socket
rc-service sshd start
rc-update add sshd default</RANGE>], consuming the remaining wall-clock time until an AgentTimeoutError [R0M.exception]. By contrast, the successful run first brought `eth0` up, obtained a DHCP lease, installed OpenSSH, and started sshd [T1B52:<RANGE>ip link set eth0 up
localhost:~# ^[[40;14Rudhcpc -i eth0
udhcpc -i eth0
udhcpc: started, v1.36.1
udhcpc: broadcasting discover
udhcpc: broadcasting select for 10.0.2.15, server 10.0.2.2

(1/11) Installing openssh-keygen (9.5_p1-r0)</RANGE>] [T1B56:<RANGE> * Starting sshd ...

Welcome to Alpine!</RANGE>], checks the failed run never reached.
